Action of the Witt algebra on categorified quantum groups
Jernej Grlj, Aaron D. Lauda

Abstract
. We construct an action of the positive Witt algebra on the categorified quantum group associated to a simply-laced Lie algebra. In the type A case, we show that this action induces an action of the positive Witt algebra on 𝔤 ​ 𝔩 n \mathfrak{gl}_{n} -foams, recovering the action of Qi, Robert, Sussan, and Wagner. We also show that this construction is compatible with the trace decategorification, inducing the action of the positive Witt algebra on the current algebra.



1.
Introduction

Triply graded link homology theories, such as the HOMFLY-PT homology
[
15
]
, often exhibit additional algebraic structure not evident in their original definitions. One example is the action of the positive half of the Witt algebra
{\mathfrak{W}}
by grading-shifting derivations, as constructed by Khovanov and Rozansky
[
16
]
. This Lie algebra is spanned by vector fields
L_{m}=x^{m+1}\frac{d}{dx}
acting by derivations of the polynomial algebra
{\mathbbm{Q}}[x]
.
Whenever link homology exhibits additional algebraic structure, such as differentials, filtrations, or Lie algebra actions, it is reasonable to expect that these reflect deeper features of the underlying categorified representation theory that govern link homology. Our results confirm this expectation for the case of the Witt algebra and clarify how this symmetry is embedded in the 2-categorical structure of the categorified quantum group
\dot{\mathcal{U}}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})
introduced in
[
17
,
12
,
28
]
.

The observation by Khovanov and Rozansky that the positive Witt algebra acts on triply graded link homology was foreshadowed by work of Gorsky, Oblomkov, and Rasmussen
[
8
]
, who showed that the stable Khovanov homology of torus knots admits an action of the Virasoro algebra. The Witt algebra arises as the semiclassical limit of the Virasoro algebra, and its appearance in this context reflects an underlying structure of derivations acting on link homology. Such structures also emerge naturally in the geometric model for HOMFLY-PT homology via coherent sheaves on Hilbert schemes of points in the plane
[
23
]
. The equivariant
K
-theory of these Hilbert schemes carries an action of the elliptic Hall algebra
[
31
]
, which contains Heisenberg and
\mathcal{W}
-type subalgebras. Together, these developments suggest that derivation operators in link homology reflect deeper algebraic and geometric symmetries and motivate the search for representation-theoretic explanations of such actions.

More recently, Qi, Robert, Sussan, and Wagner
[
24
]
defined an
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
action by derivations on equivariant
\mathfrak{gl}_{n}
homology. This work was then combined with Khovanov and Rozansky
[
16
]
positive Witt algebra action by Guérin and Roz, who constructed an action of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
on the
\mathfrak{gl}_{n}
Khovanov-Rozansky homology
[
10
]
, extending observations from
[
30
]
. This action is slightly larger than the action observed by Khovanov and Rozansky as it includes operators
L_{m}
for
m=-1
that are part of the
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
action from
[
24
]
. There is a alternative action on Khovanov-Rozansky homology presented in
[
9
]
, that action also specializes to an action of
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
.

In this article, we construct an action of the positive Witt algebra
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
on the categorified quantum group
\dot{\mathcal{U}}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})
associated to a simply-laced Lie algebra. In type
A
, our construction shows that the derivation operators observed in link homology arise naturally from higher morphisms in the categorified representation theory of
\mathfrak{gl}_{n}
, providing a representation-theoretic explanation for the appearance of Witt algebra symmetries via skew Howe duality. While skew Howe duality specifically motivates the Witt action in type
A
, our construction extends this action uniformly to all simply-laced types
\mathfrak{g}
, suggesting that the underlying derivation structure is inherent to categorified quantum groups. Some actions of
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
on KLR algebras were considered in earlier work by Khovanov
[
13
]
.

The Witt action on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}
is equivariant with respect to the action on foams and categorical Skew Howe duality. We show that this action recovers the
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
action on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
of
[
7
]
, answering a question of
[
25
]
. Moreover, we are able to show that our action is equivariant with respect to the action on current algebras and trace decategorification of Beliakova, Habiro, Webster and one of the authors in
[
1
]
, see also
[
4
,
3
]
.

2.
Preliminaries

Fix a base field
\Bbbk
. We will always work over this field, which is not assumed to be of characteristic 0, nor algebraically closed. We assume that
2
is invertible.

2.1.
Symmetric functions

Let us denote by
S_{k}
the symmetric group and
\operatorname{Sym}_{k}={\mathbbm{Z}}[x_{1},\dots,x_{k}]^{S_{k}}

the ring of symmetric polynomials.

Let
\operatorname{Sym}
be the ring of symmetric functions, defined as a subring of
the inverse limit of the system
(\operatorname{Sym}_{k})_{k\geq 0}
(see
e.g.
[
21
]
). The elementary symmetric functions

e_{j}:=\sum_{1\leq i_{1}<i_{2}<\dots<i_{j}}x_{i_{1}}\dots x_{i_{j}}\,,

or the complete symmetric functions

h_{j}:=\sum_{1\leq i_{1}\leq i_{2}\leq\dots\leq i_{j}}x_{i_{1}}\dots x_{i_{j}}

generate
\operatorname{Sym}
as a free commutative ring, i.e.,

\operatorname{Sym}={\mathbbm{Z}}[e_{1},e_{2},\ldots]={\mathbbm{Z}}[h_{1},h_{2},\ldots]
.
The power sum symmetric functions are defined by

p_{t}:=\sum_{i}x_{i}^{t}\,.

We have the Newton identities:

\displaystyle je_{j}=\sum_{i=1}^{j}(-1)^{i-1}e_{j-i}p_{i},\qquad jh_{j}=\sum_{i=1}^{j}h_{j-i}p_{i}\,.

2.2.
Witt algebra

We will define a Witt sequence and the positive half of a Witt algebra following
[
25
, Section 3]
.

Definition 2.1
.

The Lie algebra
{\mathfrak{W}}
is generated by symbols
({\mathsf{L}_{n}})_{n\in{\mathbbm{Z}}}

subject to the relations

(2.1)

\displaystyle[{\mathsf{L}_{n}},{\mathsf{L}_{m}}]

\displaystyle={\mathsf{L}_{n}}\circ{\mathsf{L}_{m}}-{\mathsf{L}_{m}}\circ{\mathsf{L}_{n}}

(2.2)

\displaystyle=(n-m){\mathsf{L}_{m+n}}

for all
n,m\in{\mathbbm{Z}}
.

The Lie algebra
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
is a three dimensional Lie algebra with generators
e,h,f
with the following relations:

(2.3)

\displaystyle[h,e]=2e,\quad[h,f]=-2f,\quad[e,f]=h

We will be interested in the Lie subalgebra
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
generated by symbols
({\mathsf{L}_{n}})_{n\in{\mathbbm{Z}}_{\geq-1}}
.

Lemma 2.2

(Lemma 3.6
[
25
]
)
.

There is an injective map of Lie algebras
\iota\colon\mathfrak{sl}_{2}\rightarrow{\mathfrak{W}}
given by:

\displaystyle\iota:\quad e

\displaystyle\mapsto{\mathsf{L}_{-1}}

\displaystyle h

\displaystyle\mapsto 2{\mathsf{L}_{0}}

\displaystyle f

\displaystyle\mapsto-{\mathsf{L}_{1}}

whose
image is in
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
. This is a maximal finite-dimensional subalgebra of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
.

Lastly, we will need the definition of a Witt sequence.

Definition 2.3
.

A
Witt-sequence

(\lambda_{n})_{n\in{\mathbbm{Z}}_{\geq-1}}\in\Bbbk^{\infty}
is a sequence such that
\lambda_{-1}=0
and for any
m,n\in{\mathbbm{Z}}_{\geq 0}
,

n\lambda_{n}-m\lambda_{m}=(n-m)\lambda_{m+n}.

Lemma 2.4
.

The Lie algebra
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
acts on the ring of polynomials in infinitely many variables
\Bbbk[z_{1},z_{2},\dots]
where the action is given as follows. Let
p\in\Bbbk[z_{1},z_{2},\dots]
, then

\displaystyle{\mathsf{L}_{n}}\cdot p=-\sum_{i}z_{i}^{n+1}\frac{\partial p}{\partial z_{i}}.

In particular, we have an action of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
on the ring of symmetric functions
\operatorname{Sym}
.

Lemma 2.5
.

Let
h_{m}
,
e_{m}
and
p_{m}
be the symmetric functions of degree
m
as defined in
2.1
. Then

\displaystyle{\mathsf{L}_{n}}(h_{m})

\displaystyle=-(n+m)h_{n+m}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}p_{n-j}h_{m+j}

\displaystyle{\mathsf{L}_{n}}(e_{m})

\displaystyle=(-1)^{n+1}(n+m)e_{n+m}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(-1)^{j+1}p_{n-j}e_{m+j}

\displaystyle{\mathsf{L}_{n}}(p_{m})

\displaystyle=-mp_{n+m}

Proof.

We will only prove the first equality; the second equality follows similarly, and the last equality is evident.
For the first equality, note that the complete symmetric functions have a generating function
\sum_{i}h_{i}t^{i}=H(t)=\prod_{i}\frac{1}{1-x_{i}t}
. It follows readily that
{\mathsf{L}_{n}}(\frac{1}{1-x_{i}t})=-\frac{x_{i}^{n+1}t}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}
, therefore

\displaystyle{\mathsf{L}_{n}}(H(t))

\displaystyle=\sum_{i}{\mathsf{L}_{n}}(h_{i})t^{i}

\displaystyle=-\sum_{i}\left(\frac{x_{i}^{n+1}t}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}\cdot\prod_{i\neq j}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}\right)

\displaystyle=-\sum_{i}\left(\frac{x_{i}^{n}-x_{i}^{n}+x_{i}^{n+1}t}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}\cdot\prod_{i\neq j}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}\right)

\displaystyle=\sum_{i}\left(\frac{x_{i}^{n}(1-x_{i}t)}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}\cdot\prod_{i\neq j}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}\right)-\sum_{i}\left(\frac{x_{i}^{n}}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}\cdot\prod_{i\neq j}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}\right)

\displaystyle=p_{n}H(t)-\sum_{i}\left(\frac{x_{i}^{n}}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}\cdot\prod_{i\neq j}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}\right)

where we used the fact that
p_{n}=\sum_{i}x_{i}^{n}
. We repeat the same process again, we additionally need to multiply the summation with
t\cdot\frac{1}{t}
(and higher powers later), to get the correct numerators.

\displaystyle=p_{n}H(t)-\frac{1}{t}\sum_{i}\left(\frac{x_{i}^{n-1}-x_{i}^{n-1}+tx_{i}^{n}}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}\cdot\prod_{i\neq j}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}\right)

\displaystyle=p_{n}H(t)+\frac{1}{t}p_{n-1}H(t)-\frac{1}{t}\sum_{i}\left(\frac{x_{i}^{n-1}}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}\cdot\prod_{i\neq j}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}\right)

\displaystyle=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}t^{-j}p_{n-j}H(t)-\frac{1}{t^{n-1}}\sum_{i}\left(\frac{x_{i}}{(1-x_{i}t)^{2}}\cdot\prod_{i\neq j}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}\right)

One last trick is to realize the terms in the summation as partial derivatives in
t
.

\displaystyle=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}t^{-j}p_{n-j}H(t)-\frac{1}{t^{n-1}}\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\prod_{i}(1-x_{j}t)^{-1}

\displaystyle=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}t^{-j}p_{n-j}H(t)-\frac{1}{t^{n-1}}\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\sum_{i}h_{i}t^{i}

\displaystyle=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}t^{-j}p_{n-j}H(t)-\sum_{i}ih_{i}t^{i-n}

So we observe.

(2.4)

\displaystyle{\mathsf{L}_{n}}(h_{m})

\displaystyle=-(n+m)h_{n+m}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}p_{n-j}h_{m+j}

∎

2.3.
The 2-category
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})

For this article, we restrict our attention to simply-laced Kac-Moody algebras. These algebras are associated to a symmetric Cartan data consisting of

•

a free
{\mathbbm{Z}}
-module
X
(the weight lattice),

•

for
i\in I
(
I
is an indexing set) there are elements
\alpha_{i}\in X
(simple roots) and
\Lambda_{i}\in X
(fundamental weights),

•

for
i\in I
an element
h_{i}\in X^{\vee}={\rm Hom}_{{\mathbbm{Z}}}(X,{\mathbbm{Z}})
(simple coroots),

•

a bilinear form
(\cdot,\cdot)
on
X
.

Write
\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\colon X^{\vee}\times X\rightarrow{\mathbbm{Z}}
for the canonical pairing. This data should satisfy:

•

(\alpha_{i},\alpha_{i})=2
for any
i\in I
,

•

(\alpha_{i},\alpha_{j})\in\{0,-1\}
for
i,j\in I
with
i\neq j
,

•

\langle i,\lambda\rangle:=\langle h_{i},\lambda\rangle=(\alpha_{i},\lambda)

for
i\in I
and
\lambda\in X
,

•

\langle h_{j},\Lambda_{i}\rangle=\delta_{ij}
for all
i,j\in I
.

Hence
(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}
is a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix, where
a_{ij}=\langle h_{i},\alpha_{j}\rangle=(\alpha_{i},\alpha_{j})
. We will sometimes denote the bilinear pairing
(\alpha_{i},\alpha_{j})
by
i\cdot j
and abbreviate
\langle i,\lambda\rangle
to
\lambda_{i}
.
We denote by
X^{+}\subset X
the dominant weights which are of the form
\sum_{i}\lambda_{i}\Lambda_{i}
where
\lambda_{i}\geq 0
.

Definition 2.6
.

Associated to a symmetric Cartan datum, define a
choice of scalars
Q
consisting of:

•

\left\{t_{ij}\mid\text{ for all $i,j\in I$}\right\}
,

such that

•

t_{ii}=0
for all
i\in I
and
t_{ij}\in\Bbbk^{\times}
for
i\neq j
,

•

t_{ij}=t_{ji}
when
a_{ij}=0
.

The choice of scalars
Q
controls the form of the KLR algebra
R_{Q}
that governs the upward-oriented strands. The
2
-category

\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})
is controlled by the products
v_{ij}=t_{ij}^{-1}t_{ji}
taken
over all pairs
i,j\in I
. When the underlying graph of the simply-laced Kac-Moody algebra
\mathfrak{g}
is a tree, in particular a Dynkin diagram, all choices of
Q
lead to isomorphic KLR-algebras and these isomorphisms extend to isomorphisms of categorified quantum groups
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})\rightarrow\mathcal{U}_{Q^{\prime}}(\mathfrak{g})
for scalars
Q
and
Q^{\prime}

[
20
]
.

Let
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})
denote the non-cyclic form of the categorified quantum group from
[
5
]
. Though a cyclic form of the categorified quantum group has been defined
[
2
]
, for our purposes, the non-cyclic variant is the most natural version. By
[
2
, Theorem 2.1]
, the cyclic and non-cyclic variants are isomorphic as
2
-categories.

Remark 2.7
.

Given an orientation of the Dynkin diagram for
\mathfrak{g}
, there is a natural choice of coefficients for
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})
where

t_{ij}=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}-1&\hbox{ if $i\cdot j=-1$ and $i\longrightarrow j$}\\
1&\hbox{ otherwise. }\end{array}\right.

This choice of parameters
Q
corresponds to the natural choice of KLR algebra
R_{Q}
that describes
{\rm Ext}
-algebras between perverse sheaves on the quiver variety
[
32
]
. In this case we have
v_{ij}=t_{ij}^{-1}t_{ji}=-1
whenever
(\alpha_{i},\alpha_{j})=-1
and subsequently
(b_{j},\alpha_{i})_{Q}=(\alpha_{j},\alpha_{i})
for all
i,j\in I
.

Definition 2.8
.

Given a choice of scalars
Q
as above, the 2-category
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})
is the graded additive 2-category with

•

Objects
objects
\lambda\in X
,

•

1-morphisms
are formal direct sums of (shifts of) compositions of

\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda},\quad\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda+\alpha_{i}}\mathcal{E}_{i}=\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda+\alpha_{i}}\mathcal{E}_{i}\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda},\quad\text{ and }\quad\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda-\alpha_{i}}\mathcal{F}_{i}=\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda-\alpha_{i}}\mathcal{F}_{i}\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda}

for
1\leq i\leq n-1
and
\lambda\in{\mathbbm{Z}}^{n}
. We denote the grading shift by
\langle 1\rangle
, so that for each 1-morphism
x
in
\mathcal{U}
and
t\in{\mathbbm{Z}}
we a 1-morphism
x\langle t\rangle
.

•

2-morphisms
are
\Bbbk
-vector spaces spanned by compositions of coloured, decorated tangle-like diagrams illustrated below.

(2.5)

\lambda+\alpha_{i}
\lambda
i

\displaystyle\colon\mathcal{E}_{i}\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}_{i}\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda}\langle i\cdot i\rangle

In this
2
-category (and those throughout the paper), we read diagrams from right to left and bottom to top. The identity 2-morphism of the 1-morphism

\mathcal{E}_{i}\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda}
is represented by an upward oriented line labelled by
i
and the identity 2-morphism of
\mathcal{F}_{i}\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda}
is represented by a downward such line.

The
2
-morphisms satisfy the following relations:

(1)

The
1
-morphisms
\mathcal{E}_{i}\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda}
and
\mathcal{F}_{i}\mathbbm{1}_{\lambda}
are biadjoint (up to a specified degree shift).

(2)

The dot
2
-morphisms are cyclic with respect to this biadjoint structure.

(3)

The
\mathcal{E}
’s (respectively
\mathcal{F}
’s) carry an action of the KLR algebra for a fixed choice of parameters
Q
.
The KLR algebra
R
associated to a fixed set of parameters
Q
is defined by finite
\Bbbk
-linear combinations of braid–like diagrams in the plane, where each strand is labeled by a vertex
i\in I
. Strands can intersect and can carry dots, but triple intersections are not allowed. Diagrams are considered up to planar isotopy that do not change the combinatorial type of the diagram. We recall the local relations.

(a)

The quadratic KLR relations are

(2.11)

Definition 2.9
.

A
2
-representation of
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})

\Bbbk
-linear

-functor
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})\rightarrow\mathcal{K}

2
-category
\mathcal{K}

3.

\mathcal{U}_{Q}

3.1.
Defining action of the Witt algebra

Throughout this section, we assume that
\mathfrak{g}
is a simply-laced Kac-Moody algebra.

Theorem 3.1
.

Let
(\mu_{n})_{n\geq-1}\in\Bbbk^{\infty}
be a Witt sequence. There is an action of the positive half of the Witt algebra
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}

\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})

{\mathsf{L}_{-1}}

n\geq 0

where we extend the action of

on composition of two morphisms

by derivations as

, the derivation property immediately implies the following Lemmas. Note that the action on the dot morphism carries a minus sign.

Lemma 3.4
.

We get the action of
{\mathsf{L}_{n}}
(for
n\geq-1
) on powersum bubbles as

\displaystyle{\mathsf{L}_{n}}\left(p_{i,m}(\lambda)\right)

\displaystyle=-m\quad p_{i,m+n}(\lambda)~.

Proof.

While this could be proved by a direct computation, we show that this is a consequence of (
2.5
). Since we know how
{\mathsf{L}_{n}}
acts on bubbles (
3.3
) and that action follows the action of
{\mathsf{L}_{n}}
on elementary and complete homogeneous symmetric functions, we may apply the fact that those symmetric functions generate the space of symmetric functions and can be used to express the power sum function via Newton’s identities (
2.1
).

The case of
{\mathsf{L}_{-1}}
needs to be treated separately as there are some
\lambda_{i}
’s appearing in
3.2
. An argument similar to the one above for the general case works. The only difference is that we need to treat
\lambda_{i}
’s as a formal variable. See
[
7
, Lemma 6.7]
for details. Note that their action of
{\mathsf{L}_{-1}}
, called
\mathbf{z}
in their work, differs by a minus sign. Additionally, the case when
m=1
is taken care of by our definition of
p_{i,0}(\lambda)=\lambda_{i}

2.26
.
∎

Remark 3.5
.

The above proof may be modified to provide an alternative proof for the action of
{\mathsf{L}_{n}}
on
e_{m}
’s from
2.5
after we establish that the action on
h_{m}
’s agrees with the action on clockwise bubbles.

3.2.
Proof of Theorem
3.1

We prove Theorem
3.1
by proving that the
{\mathsf{L}_{n}}
satisfy the relations of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
and give well-defined 2-functors on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}
. We split the proof into two lemmas.

Lemma 3.6
.

The action of
{\mathsf{L}_{i}}
’s described in Theorem
3.1
preserves the Witt algebra defining relations, so that
[{\mathsf{L}_{a}},{\mathsf{L}_{b}}]D=(a-b){\mathsf{L}_{a+b}}D
for any two morphism
D\in\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})
. Here we do not need to restrict to scalars from Remark
2.7
as we are not using any relations in the
2
-category.

Proof.

It suffices to verify the claim on generating 2-morphisms by direct computation. We will present the proof for one of the cups. The rest follows similarly. If
a=-1
or
b=-1
, the computations become simpler as
{\mathsf{L}_{-1}}
acts trivially on the majority of the generators.

), which express complete and elementary symmetric functions in terms of power sum functions and lower-order terms, along with the correspondence between bubbles and symmetric functions from Section

, one can verify that the relation holds. The mixed

) follows as a simpler special case of the same computation. Newton’s identities can also be applied to establish the bubble relation (

), using the result of Lemma

.

3.3.
Specialization to
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
and
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})

As a special case, the following proposition gives an
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
action on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
. By restricting the action from Theorem
3.1
to just
{\mathsf{L}_{-1}},{\mathsf{L}_{0}},{\mathsf{L}_{1}}
we answer a question of
[
25
]
, see the second to last paragraph of Section 4.5.

Proposition 3.8
.

There is an action of the positive half of the Witt algebra
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
. By restricting to
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
inside the positive half of the Witt algebra as in Lemma
2.2
, we get an action of
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
on the 2-morphisms of
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
that agrees with the action in
[
7
, Definition 6.13]
, see also
[
6
, Definition 4.6]
for more choices of
{\mathsf{L}_{1}}
.

Proof.

By restricting the Cartan datum of
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})
(via
I=\{1\},X={\mathbbm{Z}}
), we obtain a version of
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
, see
[
20
]
for details, hence Theorem
3.1
gives an action of the positive half of the Witt algebra on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
.

We recover some of the (degree
2
) derivations in
[
6
, Definition 4.6]
, by setting
n=1,i=1
,
\lambda_{1}=\lambda
, and
(\lambda(\mu_{1}+\frac{1}{2})-1)=-\overline{x}_{\lambda-2},-\mu_{1}+\frac{1}{2}=\overline{y}_{\lambda-2},-2\mu_{1}=a_{\lambda}
. The minus signs arise as the action of
z
in definition 6.13 of
[
7
]
on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
carries a different sign compared to
{\mathsf{L}_{-1}}
.
∎

4.
Relation Witt algebra action on foams

In this section, we examine how the action constructed in this paper arises from the foam-based action studied in
[
25
]
, via categorical skew Howe duality as developed in
[
26
]
, and generalizing earlier observations in the
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
and
\mathfrak{sl}_{3}
cases
[
19
]
.
To be precise, in
[
25
]
they work with equivariant
\mathfrak{gl}_{n}
foams of
[
27
]
. These correspond to the foams in
[
26
]
where we do not pass to the specialization described named
n\mathsf{Foam}^{\bullet}
in
[
26
, Section 4.1]
. In the world of categorified quantum groups, these foams are related, via categorical skew Howe duality, to deformed cyclotomic quotients
\check{\mathcal{U}}_{Q}^{\lambda,\ast}
of
[
29
,
33
]
. These equivariant foams are also closely related to the equivariant flag categories of
[
18
,
12
]
.

To match with
[
26
]
, we will work with
\mathcal{U}_{Q}:=(\check{\mathcal{U}}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{\infty})^{+})^{n,\ast}
using the choice of parameters from Remark
2.7
and
\mathfrak{sl}_{\infty}
root datum. Here
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{\infty})
is the direct limit of
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n})
’s, the check mark corresponds to a certain subcategory of the Karoubi envelope and the plus sign stands for the fact that we restrict the categorified quantum group to objects that are increasing in the sense that for
(\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{k})=\lambda\in X
of
•
‣
2.8
, it holds that
\lambda_{1}\leq\lambda_{2}\leq\ldots\leq\lambda_{k}
. The other subscripts indicate the restriction to the deformed cyclotomic quotient of weight
\lambda
.

We use the notation
n\mathsf{Foam}=\bigoplus_{N\geq 1}n\mathsf{Foam}(N)
for the category of
\mathfrak{gl}_{n}
ladderized foams following
[
26
]
. Since we restrict our focus to ladderized foams, we do not recover the action on the cap and cup foam from
[
25
, Equations 68, 69]
.

Our definition of the Witt action of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
is designed to be compatible with the action on foams, and this compatibility guides many of the choices made in the construction. We illustrate in the proof of Theorem
4.2
by working through several examples where the action on the categorified quantum group recovers the expected behavior under foamation.

A feature of categorical skew Howe duality is that multiple distinct foams may be mapped to the same diagram in the categorified quantum group, depending on how we represent an
\mathfrak{sl}_{m}
weight in
\mathfrak{gl}_{m}
and on the choice of ladderization, see
[
26
, Remark 2.3.3]
. We exploit this phenomenon to reduce the number of parameters, thereby ensuring compatibility with the defining relations of the categorified quantum group. Skew Howe duality also suggests that power sum bubbles should be represented using thick bubbles, as in
[
26
, Equation 3.56]
. This is equivalent to our approach via
[
14
, Equations 4.33 and 4.34]
or
[
22
, Equations 5.1 and 5.2]
, provided the bubbles are sufficiently thick (at least
n
in the image of the action of
{\mathsf{L}_{n}}
), so that the relevant determinants behave well. To avoid these technical constraints, we have opted for the definition given in (
2.26
).

Remark 4.1
.

Interpreting the power sum bubbles as thick bubbles allows one to reformulate the combinatorics of symmetric functions in terms of hook-shaped Young diagrams, offering an alternative perspective on several of our proofs.

Theorem 4.2
.

Foamation 2-functors
\Phi
of
[
26
, Section 3.2]
from
\mathcal{U}_{Q}
into the category of ladderized foams
n\mathsf{Foam}
, intertwine the action of the positive half of the Witt algebra, that is, make the following diagram commute:

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{U}_{Q}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{U}_{Q}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces n\mathsf{Foam}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces n\mathsf{Foam}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathsf{L}_{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Phi}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathsf{L}_{n}}}

Here
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
action on the top arrow for the categorified quantum group is the one from Theorem
3.1
and the action on foams is presented in
[
25
]
, fixing the parameters appearing in their work to
\lambda_{n}+\mu_{n}=0,s=\frac{1}{2}
.

Proof.

Our choice of scalars from Remark
2.7
is compatible with the choices of
[
26
]
.
Under certain conditions, Skew Howe duality becomes an eventually faithful functor, see
[
26
, Proposition 3.22]
, provided we work with
\mathfrak{gl}
in place of
\mathfrak{sl}
in
\mathcal{U}_{Q}
. The action defined in
3.1
, will descend to an action on the foams in the image of
\Phi
, if we show that changing
\mathfrak{sl}
weights to
\mathfrak{gl}
weights does not change the action

Furthermore, we will show that the action of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
is intertwined under
\Phi
. For that, we need to show that our coefficients match up with
[
25
]
. We will work with
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
weights and diagrams, the pictures can be directly realized in
\mathcal{U}_{Q}
, and the techniques extended to other morphisms in that category. We illustrate the proof by considering the action of
{\mathsf{L}_{1}}
and also clarify its relation to the construction in
[
6
]
, from the formulas given in
[
25
, Section 4.1]
. Note that the foams in
[
25
]
need not be ladderized, as mentioned above, we do not recover the action on cap and cup foams. The actions of the other operators
{\mathsf{L}_{i}}
can be recovered in a similar fashion. We adopt the notation of
[
25
, Section 4.1]
, where
s\in\Bbbk
and
(\mu_{i})_{i\geq-1},(\lambda_{i})_{i\geq-1}
are two Witt sequences.

In the notation of
[
26
, Section 3.2]
, facets colored blue are taken to have thickness
1
.
First we consider a ladderization, see
[
5
]
for a definiton, for a positive value of
\lambda
as follows

Where in the last equality, the degree
2
bubble reversed its orientation and created a minus sign according to the infinite Grassmannian relation (
2.18
), (
2.19
).

If we are to obtain an action of
{\mathsf{L}_{1}}
on the cup morphism, that is not given in a piecewise manner and does not depend on how we pass from
\mathfrak{sl}_{2}
weights to
\mathfrak{gl}_{2}
, we must demand that both actions coming from different ladderizations agree. For that to hold true, we must have that

\displaystyle\lambda_{1}+s-1

\displaystyle=-\mu_{1}-s

\displaystyle\lambda_{1}+\mu_{1}

\displaystyle=1-2s

Repeating the process for higher differentials
{\mathsf{L}_{i}}
, one sees that
s
must be equal to
\frac{1}{2}
and
\lambda_{n}+\mu_{n}=0
, using the fact that these are Witt sequences. These are all the constraints we obtain in addition to the ones above.

\Phi

Agreeing with the assignment in Theorem
3.1
. Checking the action on other cups and caps is similar, and deducing the action on upward, possibly dotted strands is straightforward.
∎

Remark 4.3
.

The above lemma and its proof show that the action on the Karoubi envelope
\mathsf{Kar}({\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})})
(that is the thick calculus) can be read from the action on foams via categorical Skew Howe duality and the presented choice of parameters.

5.
Witt actions and trace decategorifications

In this section, we restrict to
\mathfrak{g}
of ADE type and work over a field of characteristic
0
.
In
[
4
,
1
]
it is shown that the trace decategorification
\mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g}))
is isomorphic to the universal enveloping algebra of the current algebra
U(\mathfrak{g}[t])
. Furthermore, traces of natural 2-representations of
\mathcal{U}_{Q}
become representations for
U(\mathfrak{g}[t])
. In particular, the traces of cyclotomic quotients
\mathcal{U}_{Q}^{\lambda,\ast}
indexed by a highest weight
\lambda
become local Weyl modules
W_{\lambda}^{loc}
for
U(\mathfrak{g}[t])
, while the deformed cyclotomic quotients
\check{\mathcal{U}}_{Q}^{\lambda,\ast}
from
[
29
,
33
]
become global Weyl modules
W_{\lambda}
under trace dectegorification
[
1
, Theorem A.]
.
The action of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}
from Theorem
3.1
induces an action on
\check{\mathcal{U}}_{Q}^{\lambda,\ast}
.

Kac shows
[
11
]
that the Witt algebra acts as derivations on the loop algebra
\mathfrak{g}[t,t^{-1}]
via:

(5.1)

{\mathsf{L}_{n}}\cdot(x\otimes t^{m})=-mx\otimes t^{n+m},\quad x\in\mathfrak{g}.

Note that this action, when restricted to the polynomial part, agrees with the action of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
on the polynomials from
2.4
.
This action restricts to an action of the positive Witt algebra
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
on the current algebra
U(\mathfrak{g}[t])
.

Proposition 5.1
.

In characteristic
0
, the trace decategorification from
[
1
]

\mathrm{Tr}\colon\mathcal{U}_{Q}\rightarrow\mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{U}_{Q})\cong U(\mathfrak{g}[t])
intertwines the
the positive Witt algebra
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
action from Theorem
3.1
with the action from (
5.1
) making the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{g})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{U(\mathfrak{g}[t])}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{U(\mathfrak{g}[t])}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathsf{L}_{n}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Tr}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{Tr}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathsf{L}_{n}}}

commute.

Proof.

This is an immediate consequence of the fact that the trace decategorification of the action described in
2.4
agreeing with the action from (
5.1
) on the polynomial part of
U(\mathfrak{g}[t])
.
∎

While the derivations on the current algebra are somewhat intuitive, our result suggests that even this natural action can be understood as having representation-theoretic origins, all arising from the higher structure of categorified quantum groups.

Further directions

We would like to point out that our actions of
{\mathsf{L}_{1}}
do not recover all the degree
2
derivations on
\mathcal{U}_{Q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2})
as presented in
[
6
]
. One should be able to enlarge the parameter space of our action, by classifying
{\mathsf{L}_{2}}
. This might recover more of the actions of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
on foams.

The authors would be interested in extending the action of
{{\mathfrak{W}}_{-1}^{\infty}}
to an action of the whole Witt algebra or to an action of the Virasoro algebra by adding
{\mathsf{L}_{n}}
for
n<-1
.

Another point of interest is studying whether we can recover actions on
2
-representations as coming from an action on the categorified quantum groups, as we were able to do for foams or Schur qoutients with our choice of parameters. In particular, could this be related to known actions on the cyclotomic qoutients or their trace decategorifications, which are known to be Weyl modules
[
1
,
3
]
.
